title: Back to the Last Drop
summary: The trio deliberately backtracks to the Last Drop to see what became of Brannock after they left. Eva wants a control case: unlike the later setups, the first name began as an ordinary mistake. Jessie expects a town to have done whatever towns do with a good story.

panelPlan.text: The Last Drop appears from the road, visually familiar but socially altered: more people outside, Marcus's old enforcers no longer owning the porch.
Eva rehearses competing theories from the rear seat while Jessie drives. Brandon asks whether either theory changes where they are parking.
They stop short when they see a rough painted figure on the saloon wall: a black-coated Brannock cutting a rope.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: My guess: Samuel stopped at every watering hole between here and Cinder Basin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: My guess: people don't need Samuel to gossip.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You don't even know what it is.

title: Brannock Stayed
summary: The man Brandon cut down is recovering and now openly works around the Last Drop. He tells them Marcus lost control after the hanging, but the town credits 'Brannock' for the change even though Tomas knows Brandon gave a different name.

panelPlan.text: Tomas carries a tray awkwardly, rope scars still visible. He recognizes Brandon immediately and calls him Brandon, startling Eva more than another false name would.
Inside, patrons toast Brannock as the man who came back, broke Marcus's hold and vanished again; several people add contradictory details over one another.
Brandon asks Tomas whether Marcus is dead. Tomas says no; he simply left when people stopped being afraid of him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Marcus left three days after you did.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: People say Brannock ran him off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: People like a face on a story.

title: One Mistake, Twenty Stories
summary: Samuel confirms he never touched the Last Drop before Brandon arrived. Raina heard about Brannock only afterward. The near-name mistake, the old local legend and the town's own retelling created the heroic biography and political afterlife without either manipulator.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks directly whether anyone planted this first Brannock story. At a back table, Tomas sketches the chain of gossip: scarred patron to bartender, bartender to two families, two families to the workers Marcus had threatened.
Samuel confirms the seed Eva found on the first trip: name, rough description and expected day. Raina then asks who added later details and quickly runs out of clean answers.
Eva is delighted by the branching story until Jessie points out that none of the branches belong to Brandon anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Brannock is why I started asking about Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: By supper, Brannock had a dead brother.

title: The Man on the Wall
summary: Brandon confronts the crude mural of Brannock modeled on what people remember about him. Eva initially treats it as fascinating evidence; Brandon sees a version of himself the town can use without him.

panelPlan.text: Outside, Eva points out a rough hand-painted mural exaggerating Brandon into a broad-shouldered avenger with a red sun behind him; the brushwork is crude and visibly local.
Eva compares details to Brandon while Jessie watches his expression and realizes he genuinely dislikes it.
Tomas explains that the image helps people remember the day Marcus stopped owning the porch. Brandon accepts the need without accepting the identity.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Too late. They made you taller.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It isn't meant to be you exactly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: It's the day Marcus lost the porch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Does it bother you that they made him into a better version of you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: He's not a version of me. They made up somebody else and put my face on him.

title: Do Not Bless It
summary: A group of locals asks Brandon to publicly endorse their new committee under the Brannock name. Brandon refuses to bless a political arrangement as a folk hero, but he agrees to sit and hear what they are actually trying to build.

panelPlan.text: A local overhears Brandon admit what bothers him about the borrowed face and offers a solution: several locals bring a handwritten statement to Brandon, asking Brannock to sign it so Marcus cannot come back claiming authority.
Eva sees the obvious usefulness. Jessie does not answer for Brandon this time.
Brandon reads the paper, then asks each person why they need a dead or absent man to make their own agreement legitimate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: If you hate it, fix it. Just sign this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Local
dialogueInline.text: Marcus comes back, we show him Brannock backs us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: What happens when somebody else's Brannock says the opposite?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. But at least he'll know who's actually standing there.

title: Brandon Mack
summary: Tomas thanks Brandon under his real name in front of the room. The gesture is small but changes the trio: Eva has now seen a community member know exactly who Brandon is while the accidental Brannock identity continues alongside that truth. Raina has to confront that the first case she investigated never belonged to her experiment at all.

panelPlan.text: At the door, Tomas calls Brandon back and thanks him for cutting the rope. The room hears the name Brandon Mack without erupting or correcting him.
Some patrons still raise cups to Brannock. Others greet Brandon by his real name or simply shrug; both names circulate in the same room.
On the road, Eva asks Jessie whether that counts as solving anything. Jessie says it solves one thing: Brandon told the truth the first time.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: They know your name and kept Brannock.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tomas
dialogueInline.text: Some of us don't need him anymore.
